question: Which of the following best describes the strategic military-maritime approach of the Dutch Navy (VOC) in the Indian Ocean during the early 17th century?
options: Direct territorial conquest of the entire Indian mainland rather than maritime choke points
Systematic blockade of Portuguese hubs (Goa, Malacca, Macau) combined with monopolization of the spice-producing islands in the Indonesian archipelago
Forming a permanent naval coalition with the Mughal Empire to exclude all other European powers
Focusing solely on peaceful mercantile trade and avoiding the deployment of armed warships
explanation: The Dutch VOC used its superior naval force to systematically blockade Portuguese strongholds like Goa and Malacca to strangle Portuguese trade, while using military force to establish direct monopolies in the Spice Islands (Banda, Moluccas) and Ceylon.
